techniques.name: State jump cut (same screen, later state)
techniques.looks: Same page, same framing; the content jumps to its next state in one frame (prompt text appears complete, a list finishes loading, a menu item is already open).
techniques.when: Typing, loading or any wait inside one screen: he describes the action ("you just hand it a script"), the cut shows the finished state.
techniques.why: Waiting and letter-by-letter typing are dead time; the cut keeps the beat on the words without changing where the viewer looks.
techniques.how: Hard cut, 1 frame, zoom/position carried unchanged across the cut. No dissolve when the layout is unchanged.
techniques.how_often: In-span hard cuts (all kinds) 0.7–1.9 / min of screencast; state jumps are most of the non-page ones.

examples.note: prompt text appears at once (typing skipped)
Claude chat: empty box → full prompt in one cut

techniques.jake_rule: Rule 8: paste the whole domain/prompt at once, nothing pops up (suggestion lists).

techniques.name: Cut on click to the next page (load skipped)
techniques.looks: Cursor clicks a nav item/button; the next frame is the loaded destination page. White/blank loading never shows.
techniques.when: He says "click on X / head to X" and clicks; the picture lands on the result while he is still on the sentence.
techniques.why: A click inside one app means "continuing" — a hard cut reads as instant software.
techniques.how: Hard cut on (or ≤ 3 f after) the press. The incoming page usually arrives at 1.0 (or already framed if the next target is named within ~1.5 s) and then gets a push-in or pan.
techniques.how_often: Full-frame in-span hard cuts: r2 1.9, r3 1.2, r4 0.7, r5 1.7 per min (16/11/7/19 total).
techniques.jake_rule: Rule 11: a navigating click gets a quick zoom that lands on the press, then the page change; no wandering.

techniques.name: Cut chain through menus / onboarding
techniques.looks: Several hard cuts 0.7–1.5 s apart, each on a click, stepping through a sign-up form, onboarding questions or a menu tour, no camera moves between them.
techniques.when: He narrates a quick tour or a boring necessary flow ("answer honestly, it takes 10 seconds … and we're in. Images are over here, videos over here").
techniques.why: Compresses a necessary but dull flow to its milestones while staying literal.
techniques.how: Hard cuts on each click/word; zoom 1.0; 3–6 cuts in 5–8 s.

techniques.name: Hard cut screencast → full-screen narration (A-roll)
techniques.looks: Screencast and bubble vanish together in one frame; the next frame is the full-screen presenter.
techniques.when: At the end of a sentence/idea, before he starts talking about the next thing (opinion, transition, CTA).
techniques.why: The alternation screen ↔ face is the main rhythm device; it also ends most holds (37 % of all ≥ 3 s holds end on this cut).
techniques.how: Hard cut, picture leads the next sentence by ~0.1 s (median, 79–98 % of cuts within 0.6 s of a sentence start). The screencast is NOT zoomed out first: 8 / 17 / 21 / 12 spans end still zoomed (r2/r3/r4/r5), ≤ 1 per ref zooms out before the cut.
techniques.how_often: ≈ 99 % of the 134 exits (frame-checked). 1.4–3.0 exits per minute of video.
techniques.jake_rule: Rule 5: Jake asked for a very short bubble-first fade on screencast ↔ full-screen narration ("so fast it isn't noticed") — use TR05 timing, not a plain hard cut. Rule wins over the ref statistics.
techniques.correction: sc6/SYSTEM §0 rule 5 said 88 % / 94 % hard and the rest "the dissolve variant". Frame check of all 24 non-hard detections: 21 are bubble hide/return events INSIDE a screencast (BB01/BB02). True dissolve boundaries: 1 to A-roll (r3 0:47.35) + 1 bubble-first to B-roll (r5 0:35.8). So ≈ 99 % of A-roll boundaries are hard cuts.

techniques.name: Hard cut A-roll → screencast (opens at 1.0, then moves)
techniques.looks: Presenter → screencast with the bubble on frame 1. Most spans open unzoomed and still; ~30 % start a push-in or pan on frame 2.
techniques.when: When he starts the sentence that names what is on screen ("So what is VEED?", "Let me show you").
techniques.why: The face sets up the idea, the screen pays it off; starting at 1.0 tells the viewer where they are (the whole app) before the zoom isolates the subject.
techniques.how: Hard cut; first move (if any) starts at +2 f (p25–p75 2–3 f). Entry move: zoom-in 8/12/7/10, pan 3/7/3/1, none 6/19/31/23 spans (r2/r3/r4/r5).

examples.note: "So what is VEED?" → editor, push-in from +2 f

techniques.name: Cut that lands already framed (zoom carried into the cut)
techniques.looks: The first screencast frame after a cut (from A-roll or another page) is already a zoomed view, and the camera pans from there.
techniques.when: When the next thing he names is a detail the viewer already knows the context of (the same pricing table again, the same editor).
techniques.why: Skips a re-establishing push the viewer does not need.
techniques.how: Cut lands at the held zoom (≈1.25–1.37); a pan (D 30–40 f) follows within 0–2 s.
techniques.how_often: Spans that open with a pan: 3 / 7 / 3 / 1.

examples.note: cut from A-roll lands zoomed on pricing; pan to "Creator"
cut lands zoomed on the preview; glides to the timeline

techniques.name: A-roll jump cut with framing change (punch-in alternation)
techniques.looks: Inside one A-roll block, jump cuts alternate between the base medium framing and a tighter close-up (~1.3–1.5×, face larger, mic lower).
techniques.when: On a new sentence/beat inside a talking-head stretch, especially an emphatic line.
techniques.why: Hides the jump cut and adds energy without B-roll.
techniques.how: Hard cut; scale changes ~1.3–1.5× about the face. Ref 2 (oldest) keeps the same framing across jump cuts (one close-up at 5:05); refs 3–5 alternate.
techniques.how_often: Refs 3–5: roughly every 2nd–3rd A-roll jump cut.
techniques.correction: kwys-annotations C2 said "no digital punch-ins at jump cuts" — true for ref 2 only; refs 3–5 do alternate framings. | 2026-10-08 re-measure (RULEBOOK R7): across 106 presenter→presenter jump cuts in refs 2–5 the scale ratio is p10–p90 0.97–1.01; only 3 cuts changed framing ≥ 8 % (0–0.5 per presenter-minute) — alternation is NOT a reference habit; the house plan keeps the framing across jump cuts (screencast/aroll_plan.py).

techniques.name: Dissolve screencast → screencast on a change of world
techniques.looks: Short uniform cross-dissolve between two different apps/sites/projects; the facecam bubble stays solid on top.
techniques.when: Going to another app, site, window, project or account ("let's go back to the dashboard", "then over in Claude").
techniques.why: A hard cut between unrelated layouts reads as a glitch; a dissolve says "somewhere else".
techniques.how: 3–8 f (medians 3/6/5/4 → 5 f), linear opacity (+0.16–0.27 per frame), uniform over the frame. Framing of the outgoing view is held through it.
techniques.how_often: 0.4–1.4 / min of screencast; dissolves ÷ (dissolves + full hard page cuts) = 50 / 60 / 76 / 29 %.
techniques.jake_rule: Approved by Jake: v11 1:04 (dialog → brand kit dissolve).

techniques.name: Dissolve as a time skip (same page, later)
techniques.looks: Same page and framing; the generated result fades in where the empty/loading state was.
techniques.when: After "hit generate" / "a few moments later" — a generation or render finishing.
techniques.why: Says "time passed" without showing the wait.
techniques.how: 3–6 f linear; zoom HELD; usually followed within 0–5 f by a pan to the result (PN05) or a zoom-out (TR03).

examples.note: prompt → coffee video appears above it, then pan up
prompt → result (5 f), then pan up-left

techniques.name: Dissolve with held zoom, then release
techniques.looks: The new screen dissolves in at the outgoing zoom and position, then the camera zooms out to 1.0 (or glides to the new subject).
techniques.when: Arriving on an overview page after a zoomed detail ("let's go back to the dashboard").
techniques.why: Keeps the motion continuous: the zoom-out reveals the new place.
techniques.how: Dissolve 6–7 f; zoom-out starts 0–5 f after the dissolve starts, ×0.76–0.82, D ≈ 40 f, curve (.33,0,.31,.93).
techniques.how_often: Most dissolves that leave a zoomed state.

techniques.name: Dissolve screencast → A-roll (rare)
techniques.looks: Screen and bubble cross-dissolve into the presenter over ~6 f.
techniques.when: Once in four refs, at a soft sentence ("It's free to start").
techniques.why: A softer exit when the screen content continues the thought.
techniques.how: ~6 f linear, bubble fades with the screen.

examples.note: A-roll → AI B-roll clip, 8 f dissolve (kwys spec)

techniques.jake_rule: Rule 5 makes the bubble-first fast fade (TR05) the house transition for screencast ↔ narration.

techniques.name: Bubble-first exit (bubble fades, then the screen dissolves)
techniques.looks: The facecam bubble fades out first (~3–5 f), then the screencast cross-dissolves to the next full-screen shot.
techniques.when: Leaving a screencast for a full-screen shot that has no bubble.
techniques.why: The bubble disappearing first makes the screen change feel like one smooth move instead of two things popping.
techniques.how: Bubble 1→0 over ~4 f starting ~10 f before the screen dissolve; screen dissolve ~8 f (50 % at ~4 f). r5 0:35.8: bubble gone at +12 f, screen fully replaced at +16 f.
techniques.how_often: Measured once to B-roll (r5 0:35.8); the same order appears on bubble hides inside screencasts (BB01).

examples.note: Claude settings → Artlist landing (bubble out, dissolve)

techniques.jake_rule: Rule 5 (Jake): copy this for EVERY screencast ↔ full-screen narration change, both directions, "so fast it isn't noticed".

techniques.name: Graphic card fade-in / crossfade between cards
techniques.looks: A full-screen graphic plate fades up from white with the logos settling in, holds, then crossfades to the next card.

techniques.how: Fade-in ~8–16 f from white; hold ~1.5 s; crossfade ~8 f to the next card (toggle switching on).

techniques.name: Opening punch-out (video starts zoomed in)
techniques.looks: Frame 0 is the presenter punched in ~1.4–1.55×; it eases out to the base framing in ~1 s while the first title builds.
techniques.when: The very first line of the video (the hook).
techniques.why: An energetic first frame.

techniques.looks: The last A-roll frames fade to black over ~1 s; audio not faded.
techniques.when: Last word of the outro.
techniques.why: A clean end.
techniques.how: 30 f near-linear video fade, 3 black frames after (kwys C4).

techniques.name: Entry push-in (span opener)
techniques.looks: From the first or second frame of a screencast span the view pushes in toward the region the sentence is about.
techniques.when: A span opens on a screen whose subject is a part of the page (a result, a panel, a box).

techniques.looks: A gentle centred zoom on a dark list/chat/settings modal; nothing specific is targeted.

techniques.why: Re-establishes context before the next push.

techniques.name: Marker wipe on read text
techniques.looks: Yellow highlight sweeps left→right over the phrase he reads; one wipe per line; earlier lines stay.
techniques.when: He reads a phrase from the screen.

techniques.how: bezier(.264,.139,.361,.897), T = clamp(13.3+0.071·w_px, 18, 35) f; starts ~12 f after the camera starts moving to the text; exit = 19.5 f fade when the camera next moves (kwys-annotations A1).

techniques.name: Base framing + slow push-in
techniques.looks: Medium shot (head + mic, brick wall), very slow digital push-in during the block.
techniques.when: Every A-roll block.
techniques.why: Keeps the face alive.
techniques.how: Starts at 1.00 after each screencast; ~1–3 %/s linear (r2 1.8 %/s, r3 ≈ 2.8 %/s 0:08–0:13); caps ≈ 1.12–1.16 and holds (kwys C2 + re-measured). Re-measured 2026-10-08 (RULEBOOK R7): the push continues across jump cuts; long stretches are reset at sentence starts by the house plan (aroll_plan.py).
techniques.how_often: Every block. A-roll/other ≈ 26–32 % of runtime; blocks p50 5.1–6.5 s.
